title: Limiting behavior of principal eigenvalues for a class of mixed boundary value problems as the measure of the support domain goes to zero
summary: In this paper we characterize the limiting behavior of the principal eigenvalue, $\s_1[-\D,\b,Ø]$, of the boundary value problem \eqref{1.1} as the Lebesgue measure of the underlying domain, $Ø$, tends to zero. Naturally, the domains $Ø$ are assumed to be included on a fixed open set $D$ such that $\b\in\mc{C}(D)$, and they satisfy $\barØ\subset D$. Our main result establishes that, in the classical case when $\inf_{D}\b >0$, $$ \lim_{|Ø|\da 0}\s_1[-\D,\b,Ø] =+\infty, $$ whereas $$ \lim_{|Ø|\da 0}\s_1[-\D,\b,Ø] =-\infty\;\;\hbox{if}\;\; \sup_{D}\b 0$ is a constant, we can prove that $$…
